audit.why: 50.39% over 5999 games — the largest sample in this slice — and the page already frames it as a patience lane with a narrow level-2-to-3 window for you. That matches.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike describes Hijack without a cooldown, and the first-item spike claims Heartsteel plus an MR shard reduces his drain to 'a near-zero trade'.
audit.why: Hijack falls to a 30-second cooldown at rank 3, which is what makes his ultimate access a standing threat rather than a one-off. And Kingslayer heals off champions regardless of your resistances — health and MR do not stop him from restoring what you took.
audit.corrected: Rewrote spikes[1].text with the 30s figure and spikes[2].text around anti-heal instead of the near-zero claim.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sylas.json R cd 80/55/30, W text and heal flag

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and early both call his level-1 ability a 'Q heal-poke'. Chain Lash has no heal in it.
audit.why: Chain Lash lashes chains that intersect, slow, and then detonate after a delay. The heal in Sylas's kit is Kingslayer (W), which is not available at level 1 and which he must land on a champion to gain from.
audit.corrected: Fixed whys[0] and early, naming Chain Lash and putting the heal where it belongs with Kingslayer's 12s rank-1 cooldown. Abscond's 13s rank-1 cooldown added to mid.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sylas.json Q and W text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears nowhere on the page; wants.you[2] answers his sustain with an MR shard.
audit.why: The _missing rule for this matchup is needs-antiheal against Kingslayer, and it is the one purchase that changes an extended Sylas trade.
audit.corrected: Rewrote wants.you[2] and worked Grievous Wounds into early, spikes[2].text and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'dashl-less' appears as a typo in both mid and late.

edits.before: Sylas only has Q at level 1 — it is slow and wide, but he cannot dash yet. Sidestep it and you can start a charge in relative safety.
edits.after: At level 1 Chain Lash is his whole kit — a slow and a delayed detonation, no heal and no dash yet. Sidestep it and you can charge safely.

edits.before: Sylas steals your Unstoppable Onslaught with his R — he can charge your own ult into your team, so ping your jungler and keep your HP above 60% before he hits 6.
edits.after: Hijack takes your Unstoppable Onslaught and he can charge your own ult at your team — ping your jungler, hold your HP up, and note Hijack falls to 30 seconds by rank 3.

edits.before: Heartsteel + Mercs/MR shard turns his Q/W drain into a near-zero trade; your HP passive starts compounding and he cannot burst you out of the W-shield window.
edits.after: Heartsteel and an MR shard blunt his chain, but Kingslayer still heals him off you — pair the health with Grievous Wounds or he just extends the trade until it is his.

edits.before: Stack Heartsteel and MR shard so his drain heals barely register against your HP passive
edits.after: Get Grievous Wounds up before extended trades — Kingslayer is where all his sustain lives

edits.before: At level 1 Sylas has only his Q heal-poke — walk up and let him throw it, then decide if the return trade is worth it; his Q hitbox is wide but predictable, and if you sidestep it you can start a charged Q without him having any dash to escape. At level 2 he picks up his chain-dash E, and that is the true matchup start: he will try to E-stun you, then chain Q and W for a burst-heal cycle while your W is down. Pre-activate your W-shield the moment he primes the E dash, so the shield eats the magic burst and his W drain heals off a protected health bar. At level 3 you out-trade him cleanly — your W-shield negates the main damage source of his combo, and a landed charged Q stun into E armor-shred turns the trade decisively in your favor before his chain cooldowns reset.
edits.after: At level 1 Sylas has only Chain Lash — a slow with a delayed detonation at the intersection, no heal and no dash. Let him throw it, sidestep, and you can start a charged Q with nothing he can do about it. At level 2 he picks up the chain-dash and that is the true matchup start: he closes, then chains Q into Kingslayer for a burst-and-heal cycle while your W is down. Pre-activate Soul Furnace the moment he primes the dash, so the shield eats the magic burst and his heal comes off a protected health bar. Note where the sustain actually lives — Kingslayer is the only heal in his kit, 12 seconds at rank 1, so Grievous Wounds bought early turns every long trade around. At level 3 you out-trade him cleanly: a charged Q into E armour-shred settles it before his cooldowns reset.

edits.before: At levels 4-5 the lane cools into a patience game: Sylas will poke with Q from outside stun range and disengage through E whenever you look threatening, so do not charge Q in the open where he simply dashes away. Charge from brush or behind the wave, and only commit when his E is visibly on cooldown. At level 6 the matchup dynamic shifts sharply — Sylas hits R and immediately copies your Unstoppable Onslaught. His stolen version lacks your max-HP bulk behind it, so the damage and crowd-control are weaker than when you cast it, but the surprise angle is real; warn your team the moment he hits 6, keep your HP above the threshold where a stolen R engage plus his own chain cannot kill you in one rotation, and bait his E first so he is dashl-less before you start a charged Q fight.
edits.after: At levels 4-5 the lane cools into a patience game: Sylas pokes with Chain Lash from outside stun range and disengages through E whenever you look threatening, so never charge Q in the open where he simply dashes away. Abscond is 13 seconds at rank 1 — charge from brush or behind the wave and commit only once you have seen it spent. At level 6 the dynamic shifts sharply: Hijack copies your Unstoppable Onslaught, and his version lacks your max-HP bulk behind it, so it hits softer than when you cast it, but the surprise angle is real. Warn your team the moment he hits 6, keep your HP above the line where a stolen R plus his own chain cannot kill you in one rotation, and bait the E out so he is dashless before you start a charged Q fight.

edits.before: In the 2+ items phase this is a genuine 50-50 brawl: your HP wall and W-shield value scale with your Heartsteel stacks while his Q/W drain scales with AP, so the fight outcome depends on whether he can get his full chain off before you land the knockup. Build Gargoyle Stoneplate or Force of Nature as your second tank item to further blunt his magic chain, and fight on your terms — force the E dash early with a short trade, then reload the real charged Q engage once he is dashl-less. Your zombie passive guarantees you deal damage and slow him even when he kills you, which punishes any overconfident 1v1 where he burns his chain to secure the kill but dies to your reanimated form before escaping.
edits.after: In the 2+ items phase this is a genuine 50-50 brawl: your HP wall and shield value scale with Heartsteel while his chain scales with AP, so the fight turns on whether he lands the full rotation before your knockup. Build Gargoyle Stoneplate or Force of Nature second to blunt the magic, and carry Grievous Wounds — Kingslayer heals off champions, and the long trade is exactly what he is playing for. Fight on your terms: force the E dash early with a short trade, then reload the real charged Q engage once he is dashless. Your zombie passive guarantees you damage and slow him even when he kills you, punishing any 1v1 where he burns his chain for the kill and dies to your reanimated form.

notes: The page says in three places that Sylas 'E-stuns' you. Riot's Abscond/Abduct text in the kit file describes only a dash and a pull — no stun — and the kit carries no hardCC flag on E. But an empty flag means unknown, not 'no', so I did not write a correction claiming the E has no stun; where I rewrote a sentence I described what the kit does confirm (he closes and pulls) and left the question open. It is recorded in unverified and is worth one wiki check, because 'bait the E' advice reads very differently if the pull also stuns. Also worth noting for whoever runs the sylas side: no mirror audit exists yet, so the anti-heal framing here is the first pass on this pair.
